threads.body: [Testing] This `throwable == null` branch is not exercised by the added failure tests: an exceptionally completed receive supplies `null` for `message`/`messages`, so both overloads return before `setReceiveState`. Reverting this condition to the old behavior would therefore leave all new tests passing. Please add a focused test that reaches this assignment with a non-null message and a failure and verifies both that the state reports `false` and that Spring Pulsar performs the fallback consumed-message accounting.

replies.body:
Addressed in 05c7f4f0e8940fdd72d7b84de401ce54a5370cf9.

Analysis: The existing failure tests complete receive futures exceptionally, so Pulsar supplies a null message and returns before `setReceiveState`. The new unit test calls `startAndEndConsumerReceive` with a non-null message and a throwable, checks the stored accounting flag, then runs the Spring process instrumenter selected from that flag and checks the consumed-message metric.

Upsides: The test fails if the throwable guard is removed and verifies that Spring records the message when Pulsar did not.

Downsides: The Pulsar unit-test module now depends on the Spring Pulsar javaagent and javaagent-extension-api test artifacts.

threads.body: [Testing] The nested-listener regression is only covered by calling `ScopedThreadSuppression` directly in `PulsarSingletonsTest`; that unit test does not install the agent, transform `triggerListener`/`receiveMessageFromConsumer`, or verify the later receive emits no Receive span. Add an integration test using the actual Pulsar listener path where an outer listener invokes a nested listener and then receives another delivery, asserting the expected Process parents and absence of the unintended Receive span.
